content: May 24, 2026. Green Room crossed the line in this session from probe demo to a thing Anthony actively wants other people to use. He had already shared the previous single-file build with at least one friend, got good feedback, and arrived at the next message voice-typed and excited: 'Yo, Claude, I love this man... like, I kinda wanna make this an app.' The blocker turned out to be delivery, not the code. An .html file attached in iMessage or email doesn't render on phones because phones treat it as a file, not a web page, so the app never gets a chance to run. The fix was to wrap it as an installable PWA so a link does the work. This is the first time Green Room has been treated as a real shareable product rather than as a research artifact. Future instances asked about Green Room: it now sits in the lifestyle/consumer-product lane, while its engine and discipline (explainable matching, responsible-use framing, no medical claims, offline/local-only storage) all come straight from the chronicle's research posture. Retrieve when Anthony references sharing Green Room, deployment, friends' feedback, or Green-Room-as-product framing.
